tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Get the account this connection is acting as: id, email, name, timezone and where notifications reach them. Use `timezone` when creating a scheduled workflow rather than defaulting to UTC, and `id` to tell your own runs and feedback from a teammate's in lists that carry only user ids.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: List the workspaces you belong to, with your role in each. Call this first: almost every other tool needs a workspace_id from here.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Get workspace details by ID or slug, including the admin-set controls that decide what runs in it may do. `settings` is a ceiling, never a grant: a network policy there applies on top of each worker's own, and a feature switched off there cannot be switched back on per project.

tools.name: list_workspace_members
tools.description: List the members of a workspace with their role, name and join date. Use it to resolve the user ids that runs, feedback and assignments carry.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search everything in a workspace (projects, actors, checklists, interviews, automations, issues, goals, feedback, knowledge, insights, design reviews, resources, conversations) by name or content. Use it instead of listing and filtering, and before creating something that may already exist. Results

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the live projects in a workspace, most recently opened first. Call this after list_workspaces and match a target URL or product name against these before creating anything new.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Get one project (the product tracked by checklists, workflows, interviews and feedback), including its URL, audience and product description. Archived projects read as not found.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a project (a product to track with checklists, workflows, interviews and feedback). Call list_projects first and reuse a matching project rather than creating a duplicate.

tools.name: list_project_mcp_servers
tools.description: List the third-party MCP servers attached to a project and the tools each allows. Configuration only: those tools are not callable here, but an actor in a run (checklist, interview, workflow) may call the allowed tools of servers whose in_force is true. Servers are registered and attached by workspa

tools.name: list_workspace_guidelines
tools.description: List the workspace's whole library of standing rules (design system, tone of voice, brand, compliance, accessibility, shared knowledge), with how many projects hold each one. Read this before writing a rule: attaching one that already exists with `set_project_guideline` beats typing a second copy of

tools.name: add_workspace_guideline
tools.description: Add a standing rule to the workspace library. Call list_workspace_guidelines first so you do not add a near-duplicate. Attach it to the projects it applies to with `project_ids` here or `set_project_guideline` later, or set `apply_to_design_reviews` so every design review in the workspace is held to

tools.name: update_workspace_guideline
tools.description: Update a rule in the workspace library, or switch it off. Every project holding it is held to the new wording, so prefer editing the shared rule over adding a near-duplicate. Pass only the fields to change; at least one is required.

tools.name: remove_workspace_guideline
tools.description: Remove a rule from the workspace library permanently. This detaches it from every project holding it, so prefer `update_workspace_guideline` with `enabled: false` when the rule may come back.

tools.name: list_project_guidelines
tools.description: List the standing rules this project is held to: the workspace library rules it has attached. Read these before writing checks, interview guides or design feedback for the project, and assert them as observable checks rather than restating them. `attachment_id` is this project's copy of the rule; `i

tools.name: add_project_guideline
tools.description: Add a standing rule and hold this project to it (a design-system rule, a tone-of-voice rule, a compliance obligation, or shared knowledge). Every checklist run, design review, interview and triage for the project is then held to it. The rule joins the workspace library, so check list_workspace_guide

tools.name: set_project_guideline
tools.description: Attach a library rule to a project, detach it, or switch it off for this project alone. Attaching is how one workspace rule comes to hold for several projects without being retyped. `enabled: false` keeps the attachment but stands the rule down here, leaving every other project untouched. Safe to re

tools.name: list_actors
tools.description: List active actors (persistent AI user personas) in a workspace, oldest first. Prefer reusing an existing actor over creating a new one; pass an id from here to get_actor, interviews and checklists.

tools.name: get_actor
tools.description: Get an actor's details: description, system prompt, capabilities, and status. list_actor_knowledge has the knowledge it carries into runs.

tools.name: create_actor
tools.description: Create an actor: a persistent AI user persona with its own browser, email inbox (for OTP and magic-link flows), and memory. The description shapes who the persona is, so describe a person (background, goals, tech comfort), not a job title. Call list_actors first and reuse a matching actor; afterward

tools.name: update_actor
tools.description: Update an actor's name, description, system prompt, capabilities, or status. Only the fields you pass change; at least one is required. Set status to "archived" to soft-delete.

tools.name: list_actor_knowledge
tools.description: List what an actor knows, oldest first. Each entry has a kind: expertise and process entries are listed by title in every run and the actor reads one when the task calls for it; reference and account entries are found by search. Check here before add_actor_knowledge to avoid duplicates; pass an entr

tools.name: add_actor_knowledge
tools.description: Add knowledge to an actor. Choose the kind: expertise for a skill or standard it judges by in every run (brand, tone of voice, design system, compliance, accessibility), process for steps it follows, reference for facts it looks up when relevant (product docs, FAQs, policies), account for test accou

tools.name: remove_actor_knowledge
tools.description: Remove a knowledge entry from an actor permanently, so future runs no longer use it. Find the entry's id with list_actor_knowledge.

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description: List chat conversations with actors in a workspace, most recently active first, optionally filtered to one actor. Excludes the workspace assistant's conversations. Pass an id to get_conversation to read the messages.

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.description: Get an actor conversation with its full message history, oldest message first. Find conversation ids with list_conversations.

tools.name: list_checklists
tools.description: List the checklists in a workspace, with their target URL, actor, check count and a recent run. Check here before creating a new checklist: re-running an existing one keeps its history as a regression signal. Use get_checklist for the checks themselves.

tools.name: get_checklist
tools.description: Get a checklist: its target URL, instructions, run settings, every check (with the `id` update_checklist needs to edit one in place) and its 10 most recent runs. Call get_checklist_run with a run id for per-check results and evidence.

tools.name: get_checklist_run
tools.description: Get a checklist run: per-check results with evidence, score, verdict and the change since the previous run. Poll after run_checklist every 30 to 60 seconds until `status` is terminal; `outcome` is the verdict on the experience. `comparison.changes` (what got better or worse) is usually the answer wo

tools.name: flag_check_verdict
tools.description: Correct a wrong passed or failed verdict on one check: pass the result_id from get_checklist_run and a note on what was actually true. Later runs use it as calibration and re-record any code-run script; the run's own score is unchanged. Set clear to withdraw a correction.

tools.name: run_checklist
tools.description: Run a checklist (async): the actor drives a real browser through the product and judges each check, and may use the project's attached MCP servers (list_project_mcp_servers). Returns a run_id; poll get_checklist_run (runs take a few minutes). Counts against the workspace's plan and budget. Results r

tools.name: create_checklist
tools.description: Create a browser checklist: an actor exercises the product at a URL and judges each check with evidence. tools.name: update_checklist
tools.description: Update a checklist. Only the fields you pass change. Pass `checks` to replace the full set of checks, sending each existing check with the `id` from get_checklist so it keeps its run history. Changing the checks, instructions or url retires the recorded script, so the next run drives the agent afres

tools.name: delete_checklist
tools.description: Delete a checklist and its checks and runs. This permanently discards run history; prefer update_checklist, or simply not running a checklist, unless the user asks for deletion.

tools.name: list_feedback
tools.description: List the comments stakeholders and users have left on a project through the feedback widget, newest first. Each one is pinned to a page position (often to a named element) and carries device info; filter by status "new" when triaging. Use summarise_feedback to turn a list of these into themes and an

tools.name: get_feedback
tools.description: Get one feedback widget comment with its full reply thread, its page location and version, and a signed screenshot URL when one was captured. Find the id with list_feedback.

tools.name: summarise_feedback
tools.description: Summarise a project's comments into themes ranked by severity, open questions, and a self-contained implementation brief for a coding agent. Read the brief before proposing changes instead of reasoning over raw comments. The brief leaves out work an open question holds up; `answers` says which are a

tools.name: update_feedback_status
tools.description: Update a feedback widget comment's status: "reviewed" once assessed, "resolved" when confirmed fixed (ideally after a checklist run proves it), "dismissed" sparingly. The dashboard reflects the change immediately.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: List workflows (multi-step automations) in a workspace, newest first, with their triggers, whether each is active, its step count and its last run. Call get_workflow on one for its steps and the order a run takes them.

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: Get a workflow with its steps, the edges connecting them, the order a run would reach them, and recent runs. Read this before editing steps: `execution_order` is what actually runs, and any id in `unreachable_step_ids` is a step no run will ever reach.

tools.name: run_workflow
tools.description: Trigger a workflow run now (async), whatever its trigger type: it executes the stored steps (see get_workflow), which can drive browsers, post PR comments and notify members. Returns a run ID; poll get_workflow_run. Refused over the plan limit or budget cap.

tools.name: get_workflow_run
tools.description: Get a workflow run with step-level details. Poll this after run_workflow until status is terminal (completed, failed or cancelled).

tools.name: create_workflow
tools.description: Create a workflow (multi-step automation) that runs checks without anyone asking. Triggers: manual, schedule (cron), webhook, or vercel_event / github_event / cursor_event / linear_event / slack_event / figma_event so checklists re-run on deploys, pull requests, or design updates. Add steps with add

tools.name: update_workflow
tools.description: Update a workflow's name, description, or trigger. Only the fields you pass change. Syncs the Trigger.dev schedule when the cron or trigger type changes. The trigger fields edit the workflow's one trigger; a workflow with several triggers has them edited in the dashboard instead. Changing the trigge

tools.name: toggle_workflow
tools.description: Activate or pause a workflow. Scheduled workflows have their Trigger.dev schedule activated/deactivated to match. Activating a workflow that runs on a schedule, webhook or event needs the mcp:run scope, since it then starts runs on its own; pausing never does. Pausing keeps the steps and run history

tools.name: delete_workflow
tools.description: Delete a workflow and its steps and runs, and remove its schedule. This discards run history; prefer toggle_workflow to pause unless the user asks for deletion.

tools.name: add_workflow_step
tools.description: Add a step to a workflow and connect it into the run. Only stores it: nothing executes until the workflow runs. Appends by default; `sort_order` splices it in at a position. In a run, run_checklist drives a real browser; notification emails or messages members on Slack; github_comment and actor_pr_r

tools.name: update_workflow_step
tools.description: Change a step's type or config in place, leaving its connections alone (move it with reorder_workflow_steps). Only stores the change. Config shapes are as in add_workflow_step.

tools.name: remove_workflow_step
tools.description: Remove a step and close the gap: whatever led into it is repointed at whatever it led to, so the rest of the automation still runs.

tools.name: reorder_workflow_steps
tools.description: Set the order a workflow runs its steps in, as one linear sequence. Pass every step id: a list that leaves a step out is refused, since that step would be disconnected from the run (remove it with remove_workflow_step instead). This rewires the whole automation, so a branch built on the canvas (a co

tools.name: connect_workflow_steps
tools.description: Wire a step's output handle to another step, to build or repair a branch (adding and removing steps keeps the plain chain on their own). tools.name: comment_on_pr
tools.description: Post a comment on a GitHub pull request via the workspace GitHub connection. Use it to report checklist or interview results where engineers already look: a short verdict, then per-check outcomes with evidence highlights. Needs the Stunt Double GitHub App installed on the repository; call get_pull_r

tools.name: list_pull_requests
tools.description: List pull requests for a GitHub repository via the workspace GitHub connection, most recently created first (up to 30). Use it to find the PR number to pass to get_pull_request or comment_on_pr.

tools.name: get_pull_request
tools.description: Get details for a GitHub pull request (title, description, author, branches, change stats) via the workspace GitHub connection. Read it before writing a checklist for the change, then report back with comment_on_pr.

tools.name: list_interviews
tools.description: List the user interviews in a workspace, newest first, optionally filtered to one project. Returns summary rows; call get_interview for the discussion guide and participants, or get_interview_report for the findings.

tools.name: get_interview
tools.description: Get an interview with its discussion guide (sections and their items, in order) and participants with their run status. Also useful for polling progress after launch_interview; call get_interview_report for the synthesised findings.

tools.name: create_interview
tools.description: Create a user interview: AI persona participants complete tasks and answer questions against target_url, and results are synthesised into a report. target_url can be any reachable URL, including prototypes (Figma Make publish links, Claude design artifacts, v0) and preview deployments. Build the gui

tools.name: update_interview
tools.description: Update an interview’s name, target_url, research brief, status or usability questionnaire. Only the fields you pass change; pass at least one. To start a round use launch_interview rather than setting status to running.

tools.name: add_interview_section
tools.description: Add a section to an interview’s discussion guide. Sections group related items (e.g. "First impressions", "Checkout"); add questions and tasks to it next with add_interview_item, using the returned id as section_id.

tools.name: add_interview_item
tools.description: Add a question or task to an interview section (create the section first with add_interview_section). tools.description: Attach a participant to an interview. Provide either actor_id (existing actor) or persona_spec (ad-hoc persona: name, bio, traits), not both. tools.name: get_interview_participant
tools.description: Get an interview participant including their full transcript from the interview run. Use this for verbatim evidence behind a report finding.

tools.name: get_interview_report
tools.description: Get an interview's synthesised report (summary, themes, recommendations, per-question rollup), plus `usability` (UMUX or UMUX-Lite scores when asked). Poll after launch_interview until report_status is completed or failed; report is null until generated.

tools.name: launch_interview
tools.description: Launch an interview round (async): every participant runs the discussion guide against the target URL in a real browser, and may call the allowed tools of MCP servers attached to the project (list_project_mcp_servers); then a report is synthesised. tools.name: regenerate_interview_report
tools.description: Regenerate the synthesized report from existing participant transcripts (async), e.g. after adding participants. Returns the trigger run ID; poll get_interview_report until report_status is completed or failed.

tools.name: get_index_report

Defaults to the latest run (pass run_id for another); filter by provider or category. Use it to explain a low

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "add_actor_knowledge" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow.
